description: Code-Hello es un espacio que busca desarrollar herramientas y recursos que ayuden al aprendizaje de lenguajes de programación y videojuegos que incentivan el aprendizaje.
summary: Hello Mars is a browser game that puts players ages 7 to 12 in command of a four-person crew on a round trip to Mars. Players pack supplies, launch from Earth, keep the spacecraft running, and spend 20 Martian days at Gale Crater before bringing their crew and rock samples home. They have to balance life support, power, radiation protection, and communication delays. In the 2024 campaign, real NASA observations shape the hazards players face. Solar storms send the crew to shelter, and dusty conditions reduce solar power. Short cards show when events happened and where the data came from. The game makes the trade-offs of space exploration tangible through decisions players can revisit on their next mission.
details:
Code Available at: https://github.com/santiemanuel/space-apps-junior

From launch to splashdown. Before liftoff, players choose how to use the cargo hold’s limited space for supplies, spare parts, and shielding. On the way to Mars they maintain life-support systems, care for the crew, and respond to solar storm alerts. After landing at Gale Crater, they clean solar panels, make oxygen with a game-scaled version of MOXIE, and explore terrain inspired by Curiosity’s route to collect rock samples. The mission ends with Earth reentry and a report on crew health, radiation exposure, and samples returned.

How NASA data changes the mission. NASA’s DONKI archive provides dated solar storm alerts. BioSentinel and Curiosity RAD readings inform radiation exposure during flight and on Mars. Curiosity REMS observations inform heating needs and dust-related losses in solar power. NASA JPL planetary positions are used to estimate communication delays. When a historical event occurs, a “This really happened” card pauses the game and shows its date and source. This lets players connect an action they took, such as moving the crew to shelter, to a real measurement.

Designed for young players. The 2024 campaign follows historical events in order, while Free Mode samples different dates. Players can choose a mission of about 15 or 30 minutes, turn on help, and save their progress. The game is available in English and Spanish. The short missions and end-of-mission report let players try a different plan and compare the outcomes. Hello Mars was built with Phaser 4 and TypeScript, bundled with Vite, and tested with Vitest. The simulation uses archived data bundled with the game, so it makes no live data requests during a mission.
